body: Genuinely curious, because I haven't thought about it too much, but why does this have to be an additional parameter in the method, and not a new property of **PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D**?

> Genuinely curious, because I haven't thought about it too much, but why does this have to be an additional parameter in the method, and not a new property of **PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D**?

The reason I added it as a parameter rather than a property on `PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D` is because that class is also used in other queries like `collide_shape()` and `get_rest_info()`.

For example, `collide_shape()` returns points, so a `with_points = false` would conflict with its purpose. Similarly, `get_rest_info()` returns a position, so disabling that via a shared property wouldn’t make sense either.

To avoid introducing inconsistent or misleading behavior across APIs, I kept it specific to `intersect_shape()` as a method argument.

I'm running into trouble resolving the compatibility validation errors after adding a third `with_points` argument to `intersect_shape()`. I followed the steps from the official documentation [Handling compatibility breakages](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/handling_compatibility_breakages.html) by introducing `_bind_compatibility_methods()` and adding a compatibility wrapper in `servers/physics_server_3d.compat.inc`.

Despite that, the extension API validation still fails with:

```
Error: Field 'classes/PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D/methods/intersect_shape/arguments': size changed value in new API, from 2 to 3.
```

It seems the validator still detects the signature change even though the wrapper exists. I'm not sure how to proceed while keeping the method name the same.

As an alternative, I’m considering removing the `with_points` parameter entirely and always including point data in the results. This avoids the compatibility issue but introduces slight overhead in cases where point data isn’t needed.

Would love input on how best to move forward—whether there’s a better way to work around the signature change while keeping compatibility, or if always including point data would be an acceptable trade-off.

> It seems the validator still detects the signature change even though the wrapper exists. I'm not sure how to proceed while keeping the method name the same.

This is actually entirely normal. All it's being asked to do is add that line to `4.4-stable.expected`. Something like:
```
GH-106037
---------
'classes/PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D/methods/intersect_shape/arguments': size changed value in new API, from 2 to 3.

Optional "with_points" argument added.
```
In the same file you can see other API changes going through the same process
